question: Have other people extended Steven C. Bonta's work since his recent lectures?
finding: Later authors have used, criticized and adapted parts of Bonta's work. This search did not verify a systematic continuation of the phonetic and logographic value table presented in his 2025 lectures, an independently validated expansion of those readings, or a census of additional inscriptions read with the same rules.
chronology: The reviewed lecture series was uploaded in October–December 2025. Yajnadevam's inspected November 2024 manuscript predates that series and cites Bonta's 2023 proposal. The December 2025 and March 2026 computational papers cite Bonta's 2010 work. A 2026 informal diary directly comments on his lecture readings.

criteria.direct_extension: Retains identifiable Bonta sign assignments or field rules and derives additional sign values or inscription readings with an explicit evidence trail.
criteria.methodological_follow_up: Develops or tests a related distributional or lexical-search procedure, while its relation to Bonta is specified.
criteria.citation_or_reception: Mentions, endorses or discusses Bonta without demonstrating additional readings under his system.
criteria.verification_scope: Source reading only. No new corpus calculation, lexical-search replication, code execution or archaeological authentication was performed.

substantive_follow_ups.author: yajnadevam
substantive_follow_ups.title: A cryptanalytic decipherment of the Indus script
substantive_follow_ups.access: Read retained local PDF extraction and web PDF passages, including the abstract, section 2.8.1, section 4.3 and bibliography.
source_observations: PDF p. 1 describes regular expressions and set intersection, a proto-abugida interpretation and claimed readings of more than 500 inscriptions.
PDF p. 11, section 2.8.1, cites Bonta 2023 on multi-stem compounding and extends the claimed exclusion to other agglutinative languages.
PDF p. 26, section 4.3, says its results differ markedly from earlier decipherment proposals while claiming support for selected earlier findings.
PDF p. 94 gives the Bonta 2023 bibliography entry.
substantive_follow_ups.relationship: Explicit use of Bonta's language-selection argument within a different proposed reading system. This is evidence of uptake of an argument, not a demonstrated continuation of his sign table.
substantive_follow_ups.limitation: The inspected version predates the 2025 lectures. Its claimed readings and exclusion of language families are author claims; this review did not validate them.

related_code.observation: The README describes manually constructed regexes, dictionary normalization and augmentation, and repeated substitution across inscriptions. It presents a demonstration of sequential assignment rather than an implementation of Bonta's value table.

substantive_follow_ups.title: A Computational Analysis of the Indus Script: Identifying Sign Functions in Logo-Syllabic Writing Systems
substantive_follow_ups.access: Read publisher metadata and selected sections of the four-page publisher PDF and author-uploaded text. This expands the previous abstract/reference-only access record without changing that earlier record.
source_observations: Printed p. 19, introduction, cites Bonta 2010 as one source for the logo-syllabic interpretation.
Printed pp. 19–20 expand singleton sign candidates by shared contexts and evaluate frequent pairs.
Printed p. 21 compares co-occurrence vectors, clusters signs and pairs, and filters proposed syllabic pairs by contextual exclusivity.
Printed p. 22, reference 7, identifies the cited Bonta work as The Indus Valley Script: A New Interpretation (2010).
substantive_follow_ups.relationship: Related computational classification and clustering that cites Bonta's earlier structural work. It does not carry forward the proposed sounds and words from his 2024 manuscript or 2025 lectures.
substantive_follow_ups.limitation: The main procedural precedents also include Wells, Fuls, Sinha and Parpola. The citation does not establish that the procedure was derived specifically from Bonta. Reported semantic classes were not independently reproduced here.

substantive_follow_ups.author: Louis L. Merriam
substantive_follow_ups.title: Identifying Candidate Syllabic Sign Pairs in the Indus Script: A Computational Analysis of High-Frequency Sign Pairs
substantive_follow_ups.access: Read author-upload metadata and selected substantive text: introduction, methods, candidate search, conclusion and references.
source_observations: Printed p. 3 discusses Bonta's objections to a Dravidian interpretation, including compounding and doubled signs. It proposes other possible explanations for those observations.

Printed pp. 8–9 discuss Wells signs 705/706 with the three-stroke sign 033. The paper attributes a syllabic-pair interpretation to Bonta and reports that other numerals occur in the same context, weakening the exclusivity argument.
Printed pp. 10–12 describe weighted Euclidean distances between preceding and following context profiles, adapting Fuls's method using an ICIT February 2025 data export.
Printed pp. 18–20 generate Proto-Dravidian lexical candidates and present them as a shortlist requiring additional evidence.
Printed p. 22, reference 10, cites Bonta's 2010 work. The paper does not cite his 2025 lecture series.
substantive_follow_ups.relationship: Direct critical engagement with arguments attributed to Bonta, accompanied by a computational candidate-generation method. It uses a Proto-Dravidian working hypothesis and does not extend Bonta's Sanskrit sign assignments.
substantive_follow_ups.limitation: The attribution of recent compounding arguments is not backed by a separate citation to the 2023/2024 proposal in the inspected bibliography. The numeral counterexample and numerical outputs remain the author's reported observations; no corpus replication was run.

substantive_follow_ups.author: Celeste Claire Horner
substantive_follow_ups.title: Current Projects Closet. Development Diary
substantive_follow_ups.date_evidence: The page contains July–October 2026 entries. Its linked main draft identifies the author and records access to Bonta's 2024 manuscript on 2026-07-14.
substantive_follow_ups.access: Read dated diary passages responding to Bonta's lecture values and the main page's author identification and bibliography. Embedded inscription images were not visually audited in this review.
source_observations: The diary compares Bonta's proposed sign values with the author's own readings, including proposed pati, jar, wealth and divine-name interpretations.
The author proposes religious and mythological interpretations, records disagreement with Bonta on votive versus asset contexts, and links specific lecture moments.
The main page attributes the work to Celeste Claire Horner and cites Bonta's 2024 second edition.
substantive_follow_ups.relationship: Informal adaptation and comparison directly responding to lecture readings. It provides a public non-academic follow-up, but this review found no audited application of Bonta's complete rules to an independently evaluated set of inscriptions.
substantive_follow_ups.limitation: Later mythology and pictorial parallels are hypotheses requiring dated archaeological support and comparative controls. The diary's decipherment language is the author's claim.

other_checked_leads.author: Archana Das
other_checked_leads.title: Significance of Indus stamp-seals in ancient world trade
other_checked_leads.access: Read title, abstract, methodology, relevant source passage and bibliography.
other_checked_leads.classification: Uses Bonta 2010 as a descriptive source about seals and inscriptions; no extension of the recent sign table found.

other_checked_leads.author: Adithyan Madhu
other_checked_leads.title: Linguistic Lineages and Lost Scripts: A Cross-Civilizational Analysis of the Indus Valley Script
other_checked_leads.access: Read author/date declaration and passages matching Bonta and Yajnadevam.
other_checked_leads.classification: Not usable as evidence of a Steven Bonta extension: the matching bibliography attributes its item to Paula Bonta, 1983. That reference was not independently authenticated.

other_checked_leads.title: An Interview with Asko Parpola
other_checked_leads.access: Read the discussion of current decipherment work and the Bonta exchange.
other_checked_leads.classification: Reception and discussion of competing approaches. The skeptical assessment of Bonta in the exchange is spoken by interviewer Omar Khan; it must not be silently attributed to Parpola.

other_checked_leads.title: Indus-CoT: Chain-of-Inference Framework
other_checked_leads.access: Read source links and chronology, then followed the Rao citation.
other_checked_leads.classification: A generated literature grouping, not a newly verified method bearing that name. Its statement about extending Wells and Bonta points to Rao 2018, which predates the recent lectures.

other_checked_leads.title: The Indus Script

other_checked_leads.classification: Unresolved author-essay lead referring to Bonta 2010; not counted as a verified extension.

other_checked_leads.title: Bulletin of the IRC No. 6, June 2025

search_scope.limitations: Publicly indexed sources and retained project witnesses were checked. Some name-only searches returned unrelated California legal material. No private correspondence, inaccessible lecture comments or unindexed manuscripts were reviewed. Failure to find a direct extension is not proof that no such work exists.
search_scope.next_review_inputs: A dated paper, code repository or collaborator report that identifies retained Bonta assignments, adds values or readings, gives the complete attempted object set and explains its validation would change the direct-extension finding.
